page: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v7 is a general purpose virtual machine based on 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor. It does not incorporate hardware accelerator devices such as discrete graphics processing units.

The instance is provisioned without local disk storage, meaning all operational data and root volumes must reside on remote network volumes. It supports Azure Premium Storage, allowing storage throughput and capacity to scale independently via managed disks. Furthermore, the virtual machine does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual network interfaces and network gateway configurations for external connectivity.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated arm64 core allocation paired with proportional memory provides predictable computational density for environments optimized for ARM execution. Omitting integrated local disks and specialized accelerator hardware keeps resource overhead focused strictly on memory and compute capacity. The D32ps_v7 is well aligned with horizontally scaled web serving, relational and key-value databases using network storage, continuous integration pipelines, and general enterprise application backends compiled for ARM architectures.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v7 is a general purpose virtual machine built on the 64-bit ARM architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The configuration includes no local storage disks, relying on external Premium Storage attachment for operating systems and persistence, and contains no discrete hardware GPU accelerators. With its dedicated core allocation and balanced resource profile, the D32ps_v7 offers predictable resource density for ARM-native architectures. This configuration delivers cost-efficient multi-threaded compute without the overhead of unneeded local disk arrays or accelerator hardware. It is appropriate for general purpose enterprise workloads, application backends, web serving tiers, and containerized microservices compiled for arm64 execution.
